import pandas as pd

def main():
    # Define source file paths
    source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_39/test_0.csv"
    source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_39/test_1.csv"
    
    # Load source tables
    df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path)
    df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path)
    
    # Inspect and clean Source0 (Source1_39_0)
    # Rename columns to avoid collision after join
    # Source0 columns: ['State', 'Participation', 'English', 'Math', 'Reading', 'Science', 'Composite']
    # Rename Participation -> Participation_x, Math -> Math_x
    df0_renamed = df0.rename(columns={
        'Participation': 'Participation_x',
        'Math': 'Math_x'
    })
    
    # Inspect and clean Source1 (Source1_39_1)
    # Source1 columns: ['State', 'Participation', 'Evidence-Based Reading and Writing', 'Math', 'Total']
    # Rename Participation -> Participation_y, Math -> Math_y
    df1_renamed = df1.rename(columns={
        'Participation': 'Participation_y',
        'Math': 'Math_y'
    })
    
    # Merge on 'State' column (inner join to keep only states present in both)
    merged = pd.merge(df0_renamed, df1_renamed, on='State', how='inner')
    
    # Select and reorder columns to match target schema:
    # ['State': string, 'Participation_x': string, 'English': float, 'Math_x': float, 'Reading': float, 'Science': float, 'Composite': float,
    #  'Participation_y': string, 'Evidence-Based Reading and Writing': integer, 'Math_y': integer, 'Total': integer]
    
    # Convert datatypes accordingly:
    # Participation_x, Participation_y: string (already string with %)
    # English, Math_x, Reading, Science, Composite: float
    # Evidence-Based Reading and Writing, Math_y, Total: integer
    
    # Ensure numeric columns are properly typed
    float_cols = ['English', 'Math_x', 'Reading', 'Science', 'Composite']
    int_cols = ['Evidence-Based Reading and Writing', 'Math_y', 'Total']
    
    for col in float_cols:
        merged[col] = pd.to_numeric(merged[col], errors='coerce')
    for col in int_cols:
        merged[col] = pd.to_numeric(merged[col], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')  # Nullable integer dtype
    
    # Select columns in target order
    target_columns = [
        'State',
        'Participation_x',
        'English',
        'Math_x',
        'Reading',
        'Science',
        'Composite',
        'Participation_y',
        'Evidence-Based Reading and Writing',
        'Math_y',
        'Total'
    ]
    
    target_df = merged[target_columns]
    
    # Write to target CSV
    target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_39/target_multisource_cot.csv"
    target_df.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
